svg.text: Repaso — the four graphs, edge by edge
Nodes in execution order, every conditional edge drawn and labelled, and the exit each refusal takes. Nothing here is implied.
a terminal exit — the graph stops here
no competency match in the taxonomy
critic or blind probe killed each
Every happy-path edge carries the same condition — run.terminal is None. A terminal exit sets it, and the graph stops without a special node.
generate and validate each take claim("stage#<material>#generate") before spending. After a crash the graph re-enters, loses the claim, and reads the finished
items back from the store instead of calling Sonnet a second time. Every terminal exit above fires before a single generate or judge token is billed.
a session already exists for today
SM-2 returns no item for today
→ no message is sent at all
Session + response together are the tutor loop
One EventBridge schedule per family fires daily_session_due; the session graph plans a capsule, delivers it, and goes quiet. Every reply the parent
forwards re-enters through the response graph in the band below. Neither graph polls, and neither runs twice for the same student on the same day.
Exam mode: an EXAM# date inside 7 days caps the capsule at 4 items and re-orders them weakest-EMA first — the agent then rewrites its own schedule.
Silence is a legal output. No item due means no message: this system is not required to speak to a family every day.
Demo clock: 30 students × 14 days = 420 student-days through these same graphs in ~14 s, $0, byte-identical per seed; 1,062 responses graded.

result. No model runs on this node.

The hard rule — the model can neither veto the interrupt nor manufacture one.
build_signals() computes struggle, disengagement and fast-guessing from core.harness.escalation_triggers before any model call, and fallback_decision()
turns them into an action. If a trigger fired, decide() returns that action and drops Haiku's reply unread; if the Bedrock call fails, the same action stands.
is claimed once per ISO week
it may ask for. An unresolved item
ISO week. The prompt gets no alias.
retires the item. No model votes.
Close runs verify → engagement → cohort → optimize on unconditional edges: the conditions live inside the nodes as preconditions, not on the graph. Every message it can send is
claimed once per ISO week (engage#<student>#2026-W34, and one claim per section+competency), so a re-run of the close is silent rather than a second alert to the same family.

A guard proposed to cut the residual struggle false positives — a corroboration floor — was falsified by its own pre-declared protocol (recall fell 0.994 → 0.917) and reverted. The real fix, a BKT-style estimator, is roadmap.
The school calendar cannot fool it
genuine dropouts still caught at 3 practicable
the pre-fix control arm still fires 1,689 alerts
Execution limits are set on every graph — ingest 8 · session 4 · response 6 · close 6 node executions. A graph that loops stops; it does not spend.
Built with strands.multiagent.graph.GraphBuilder: deterministic nodes are MultiAgentBase subclasses and every conditional edge closes over a typed run context, so each branch is unit-testable.
Sources — armor bench 2026-08-20 · calibration validation 2026-08-20 · calendar gaps 2026-08-21 · demo clock 2026-08-20. 706 offline tests, ~5 s, zero credentials, zero network.
